input.cmd:
sed -i 's/`resolve_expr_image` evaluates a path-named subtree/`resolve_expr_base` evaluates a path-named subtree/' .caos-expr
sed -i 's/`resolve_expr_image` evaluates/`resolve_expr_base` evaluates/' std/.caos-expr
grep -n 'resolve_expr_image' .caos-expr std/.caos-expr || echo "updated"

content.text:
#
# `std/deep-deps` is named BY PATH, and that is what breaks the cycle:
# `resolve_expr_image` evaluates a path-named subtree against ITSELF, so it sees
# `std/deep-deps`'s own `.caos-expr` — the `docker://seeded-deep-deps` sentinel
# the core-seeder-runner answers — and never re-enters this expression. Nor does
# the result: `eval_path` descends into what an expression produced without
# re-checking that result's own root, so the deepened tree's copy of this file
# is inert.
#
# This works only because every dependency a directory names is IN the tree.
